title: HIV-MTB co-infected patient1
characteristics_ch1: cell type: peripheral blood mononuclear cell
extract_protocol_ch1: Peripheral blood (10 mL) was drawn from the 6 enrolled patients using purple EDTA tubes, and the samples were transported on dry ice as quickly as possible. In addition, peripheral blood (10 mL) was collected from 3 healthy male volunteers aged 25 years in the morning while fasting, resulting in a total of 9 peripheral blood samples.Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated.

We employed the MobiNova®-100 Single Cell System (MobiDrop (Zhejiang) Co., Ltd.) for single-cell sequencing library preparation. The quality-controlled single-cell suspension was loaded onto a system-specific microfluidic chip along with beads pre-coated with universal cell barcodes and unique molecular identifiers (UMIs). The microfluidic system within the chip precisely controlled the fluid flow at the oil–water interface, and through droplet generation technology, individual cells were co-encapsulated with a single barcode bead in a water-in-oil droplet. Inside the droplets, cells were rapidly lysed by lysis buffer, releasing intracellular mRNA. Because the beads were functionalized with oligonucleotides carrying poly(dT) primers, these primers specifically bound to mRNA molecules with poly-A tails.
